requirement: Each assessment’s usage record MUST report its validator’s `prepared_inputs` and `delivered_inputs` under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.UsageStats`. It MUST also report the invocation count and total result bytes for each invoked tool under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.calls` and {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.result_bytes`.
rationale: In `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[terminal_provider_failure_retains_the_retry_and_undelivered_inputs]`, replace the weak `assert!(stats["prepared_inputs"].as_u64().unwrap() > 0)` with an exact check. Derive the opening-message input count the way the sibling tests do. They parse the `# Mandatory inputs` array and add the fixed three extra inputs. Then assert `prepared_inputs == count + 3`. Also assert that `prepared_inputs` exceeds `delivered_inputs` by exactly `count`, so the inputs the provider never accepted stay prepared but undelivered. — `requirements.authoring.usage_inputs` requires the usage record to report `prepared_inputs` and `delivered_inputs` as `requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.UsageStats` defines them. That definition says that if the provider fails permanently before replying, the opening inputs are counted as prepared and not as delivered. The only test that covers this permanent-failure case is the one named above, and it only asserts `prepared_inputs > 0` and `delivered_inputs == 3`. The three delivered inputs presumably come from a successful extra attempt. The run records 3 attempts but the server sees only 2 chat requests, and I did not confirm this against the code. A faulty implementation could drop the undelivered opening inputs from `prepared_inputs`, leaving it at 3, or count some of them wrongly. That implementation would still pass, so the test does not enforce the prepared-but-undelivered obligation. No other reviewed test covers this case. The retry-success and normal-delivery tests all end with `prepared_inputs == delivered_inputs`.

text: Each assessment’s usage record MUST report its validator’s `prepared_inputs` and `delivered_inputs` under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.UsageStats`. It MUST also report the invocation count and total result bytes for each invoked tool under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.calls` and {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.result_bytes`.

`UsageStats` exposes the following totals. `attempts` counts each request sent to the provider once. `retries` counts attempts that repeat a failed request. `failed_attempts` counts attempts that returned a provider error, including those followed by a successful retry.

`prepared_inputs` counts inputs prepared for agent messages. Each node inserted in the opening message counts once. Each requested `read_node` page and each `outgoing_edges` result counts once, including repeated reads. A requested search page counts one input per excerpt on that page. Source listings, search finalization, and opaque custom-tool results contribute zero.

`delivered_inputs` counts those inputs when the provider first responds successfully to the request carrying them. Each input counts once across retries and subsequent turns that replay the same conversation history. For example, if the opening message supplies three nodes and the provider fails permanently before replying, usage records three prepared inputs and zero delivered inputs.
Each invocation increments the tool’s `calls` by one, including an invocation that returns an error. Skipped calls leave usage unchanged.

Each invocation adds the UTF-8 byte length of its result text to the tool’s `result_bytes`, measured before the provider encodes the request. Error messages count by the same rule. An invocation that produces no result text adds zero bytes.

output.rationale:
`requirements.authoring.usage_inputs` has no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. Its clauses specify only what an assessment's usage record reports.

- "MUST report its validator's `prepared_inputs` and `delivered_inputs` under UsageStats": this names the values and where they are reported. Suppose the record held the same numbers in a differently organized internal structure, and they still appeared in the reported `UsageStats` fields. The observable behavior would be the same and the clause would still hold. The `UsageStats` struct, its fields and its trait impls are prescribed by the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.UsageStats`. That requirement is cited here for context, so it is not an obligation of this one.
- "MUST also report the invocation count and total result bytes for each invoked tool": the `calls` and `result_bytes` semantics are defined by the cited `ToolUsage.calls` and `ToolUsage.result_bytes` requirements. Those are behavioral counting rules, and they are judged on their own declarations.

The requirement has no implementation edges and no review roots, and it names no required library, algorithm, signature or delegation interface. The requirement has test edges, and behavioral coverage belongs to the behavioral criterion.
